speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a history of gait and limb ataxia; to begin my assessment, please describe exactly how your walking difficulties started and if they have progressed over time. REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, and Vitamin B12 levels.

speaker: Doctor
text: The initial laboratory results for your blood count, metabolic panel, and Vitamin B12 are normal. Can you describe any specific symptoms you experienced *before* the onset of your gait and limb ataxia, such as vision changes, hearing loss, or balance issues?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: The patient reports a recent onset of a "drunk-like" gait and clumsiness specifically on the right side of the body. Given your significant medical history and these unilateral neurological findings, have you ever experienced any weakness, numbness, or speech difficulties on the right side, or any episodes of fainting? REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain.

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML).

The combination of subacute, asymmetric gait and limb ataxia, your history of Crohn's disease requiring natalizumab, and the exclusion of metabolic causes strongly suggests PML. I am requesting the MRI images to confirm the presence of non-enhancing white matter lesions.
